answer: Each beacon drives a ferrous stake into a dune crest and measures its declination in the dune's iron sand; declination, depth and beacon ID hash into the next block. A reading counts only if declination sits inside the dune field's seasonal band and the stake shifted under 2 cm since last epoch. Then the beacon recites a 14-line sonnet, each line ending on the day's declination — a poem only the dune can dictate. Faking 1,000 costs $120,000 in survey rigs and $35,000 in desert runs, plus 150 POA bonded per beacon, slashed on mismatch — like forging love letters the desert never wrote.
